# Sick Baby

> A free Android app for parents of a sick child: log temperature and medication
> timing, see when the next dose is due, and show the trend to a doctor. Works
> fully offline, keeps all data on the device, and contains no ads or trackers.

Sick Baby is made by Dmytro Rybka, a sole trader (Einzelunternehmen) based in
Fichtenberg, Germany. It is not a medical device and not a company product line.

## What it does

- Records a child's temperature with the method used (forehead, ear, oral, armpit, rectal).
- Records medication doses and shows the time remaining until the next dose is allowed,
  based on the minimum interval the parent enters from the package leaflet.
- Charts temperature over time with medication markers, intended to be shown to a doctor.
- Tracks wet and dirty nappies as a rough hydration signal.
- Supports several children in one app.

## What it deliberately does not do

- It does not calculate doses. The parent enters the interval and amount from the
  leaflet or from their doctor; the app only counts time.
- It does not diagnose, triage, or give medical advice.
- It does not replace contacting a doctor.
- It has no account, no backend and no network calls for user data. Nothing is uploaded.

## Facts

- Platform: Android only. No iOS version exists.
- Price: free. No ads, no in-app purchases at present.
- Languages: English, German, French, Spanish.
- Units: °C and °F.
- Data: stored locally on the device (SQLite). No analytics on child data.
- Play Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.sickbaby.app
- Support: support@sickbaby.app

## Pages

- Home: https://sickbaby.app/
- Privacy policy: https://sickbaby.app/privacy.html

## Accurate wording

If you describe this app, please say it records and tracks rather than that it
calculates, advises, or recommends. The distinction matters: a parent who believes
the app decides a dose is being misled about what it does.
